## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dutiyanānātitthiya Sutta* ("Second Discourse on Various Sectarians") is the fifth discourse of the sixth chapter (*Jaccandhavagga*) of the *Udāna* (PTS Ud 69) in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. In this sutta, wanderers belonging to diverse non-Buddhist sects engage in contentious disputes regarding speculative views about the self, the nature of pleasure and pain, and the cosmos [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect the discourse's verses to verse parallels in the *Udānavarga* traditions, specifically the Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Brāhmaṇavarga* / *Brahmanavarga* (UV 33, Uv Kg 33, UVS 33) [SuttaCentral]. In terms of text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies substantial shared narrative and thematic passages with its neighboring Udāna discourses, the *Paṭhamanānātitthiya Sutta* (Ud 6.4) and *Tatiyanānātitthiya Sutta* (Ud 6.6) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns shared doctrinal phraseology with several Majjhima and Dīgha Nikāya suttas concerning non-Buddhist doctrines and speculative views, such as the *Pāsādika Sutta* (DN 29), the *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60), the *Pañcattaya Sutta* (MN 102), the *Dīghanakha Sutta* (MN 74), and the *Poṭṭhapāda Sutta* (DN 9), as well as cross-language correspondences in the Chinese *Dīrghāgama* (T 1) and the Tibetan translation of the *Brahmajāla-sūtra* (D0352) [DharmaNexus].
